name: Shinagawa
description: Shinagawa and Takanawa from open data, lit by the real sun: the station between the Takanawa hills and Konan's towers, Takanawa Gateway's folded roof, and the old Tokaido's first post town at Kita-Shinagawa.

imagery.attribution: Geospatial Information Authority of Japan (GSI) seamless aerial photographs (GSI terms of use, source attribution)

terrain.attribution: GSI Fundamental Geospatial Data DEM5A, 5 m airborne laser survey bare earth (GSI terms of use); 10 m DEM where 5A is absent

terrain_check.name: GSI elevation API (1 m laser DEM where flown, otherwise DEM5)

plateau.attribution: MLIT Project PLATEAU Tokyo 23 wards LOD2 building models (CC BY 4.0), as vector tiles by indigo-lab (MIT)

seawall.note: The rivers' and the bay's revetments and the castle moats: granite blocks and concrete.

trees.note: Species are not mapped, and the shared trees have no ginkgo or cherry, so the mix stands in: elms for the zelkovas, plane trees for the street planes and ginkgos. A guess, not a survey.

minor_labels: グランドプリンスホテル新高輪

tour.title: Shinagawa, from open data
tour.text: {buildings} buildings. {share:plateau}% of the footprint area stands at a height Project PLATEAU surveyed, on GSI's 5 m laser-scanned bare earth.

tour.title: Takanawa Gateway
tour.text: The Yamanote line's newest station, 2020, its roof folded like paper, on the rail yard that is becoming a new quarter.

tour.title: Shinagawa-shuku
tour.text: The old Tokaido's first post town south of the Yatsuyama bridge, its shops and lanterns. The signs here are typical of the street, not its real shops'.

sources.landmarks: Takanawa Gateway Station (Kengo Kuma, 2020; East Japan Railway Company) on OpenStreetMap's footprint, its folded roof from photographs; the old Tokaido on OpenStreetMap's line. The post town's signs are indicative: typical trades, no real shops' signs.
sources.fonts: Signs drawn with Google Fonts under the SIL Open Font License: Zen Kaku Gothic New, Shippori Mincho

night.note: The post town's signs and lanterns and the station's roof are lit landmark meshes (city.py); the streets' lamps are the country's defaults.

weather.source: Tokyo (Kitanomaru Park): Japan Meteorological Agency, 1991-2020 normals, days with at least 0.5 mm

game.title: Shinagawa on Foot
game.blurb: Walk Shinagawa under the real sun: out of the Konan exit among the towers, up the tracks to Takanawa Gateway's folded roof, and south over the Yatsuyama bridge to the old Tokaido's post town.

npcs.name: Kenji 健司
idle: Eight in the morning, the passage to the Konan exit is a river of grey suits. There's a famous photograph of it.
The Shinkansen to Osaka stops here; the airport trains too. Everyone passes through Shinagawa. {time}.

npcs.name: Asuka 明日香
idle: Inside, the roof lets the daylight through. On a sunny day you don't need a single lamp.
The old embankment they found here was the first railway in Japan: 1872, on the sea. {sun_line}

npcs.name: Masa 雅
npcs.role: Sweet shop owner 和菓子屋
idle: Shinagawa-shuku: the first night out of Edo on the Tokaido. Inns, teahouses, and travellers saying goodbye.
My family has made sweets on this road for five generations. The road's older.

npcs.name: Kaori 香織
idle: An aquarium in a hotel: dolphins, a jellyfish room, and a tunnel of sharks.
At night the dolphin show has lights and music. Book ahead.

quests.title: Shinagawa
talk: Welcome to Shinagawa. Konan's towers along the canal this side, hotels and hills across the tracks.
Walk up to Takanawa Gateway, the new station. Asuka can show you around.

quests.title: Takanawa Gateway
talk: Look at the roof: white membrane on timber, folded.
The whole rail yard here is becoming a new town. Come back in ten years.

quests.title: Shinagawa-shuku
talk: The Tokaido, the old road to Kyoto. Walk along it a little.
Then go and see the dolphins up the hill, at the hotel. Kaori works there.
